transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, I came in because I’ve been making these small mistakes that are starting to be a problem. Like I’ll turn in applications or research notes thinking I checked them, and then later I notice something embarrassing, like a mislabeled artwork date or even a skipped question. It’s not huge every time, but it keeps happening enough that I’m worried about it.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention on tasks, even when you want to focus?

Yeah, I do. If I’m reading or trying to write at my desk, it doesn’t take much to pull me off track. Like a siren outside, or someone talking in the hallway, or even just a random thought about an exhibit idea. Then I’ll kind of follow that, and it can be twenty minutes before I realize I stopped doing the original thing.
Did these attention problems start when you were a child?

Yeah, I think so. Even back in elementary school, teachers would say I had good ideas, but I’d forget to turn in worksheets or lose the instructions. I remember my parents having to check my backpack every night, because otherwise I’d miss little details or just not hand something in.
As a child, were you often fidgety or unable to stay seated when you were expected to?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember being especially fidgety or always getting out of my seat as a kid. That wasn’t something teachers or my parents brought up much, at least not that I know of.
Do these attention problems also cause difficulties outside of school or work, like at home or in daily life?

Yeah, it does. It’s not just school stuff. I’ll mean to do normal things, like return an email, pay a bill, or pick up groceries, and then a few days later I realize I just never did it. It kind of just drops out of my mind unless I write it down or something reminds me.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about stuff sometimes, like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I spend a lot of time worrying about a bunch of different things when nothing’s really happening.
Do you get unwanted thoughts or feel driven to repeat behaviors like checking things over and over?
No, not really. I don’t think I have unwanted thoughts like that, and I’m not driven to keep checking things over and over.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent pattern of inattention with careless mistakes, distractibility, difficulty sustaining attention, and forgetfulness affecting academic/work and home functioning. Symptoms were present since childhood and occur across settings. Hyperactive-impulsive symptoms are not supported, making attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive type, the best fit. Anxiety and obsessive-compulsive explanations were not supported by the interview.
